analyst_view.overall: Early view: a bottom-five meeting between Genclerbirligi (14th, 11 pts) and Gaziantep (16th, 8 pts), who have lost six league games in a row and parted with coach Orhan Ak on 7 November with no successor named yet. Bernd Storck's side lost 3-0 at Besiktas after Metehan Baltaci's early red card, and they are also without Ousmane Diabate (fifth yellow), while defender Thalisson went off injured in that game. A new coach in the Gaziantep dugout could change the picture, so this will be refreshed with team news.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. I lean higher: Gaziantep have conceded 14 goals in their last seven matches and are in the middle of a coaching change, while Genclerbirligi scored five at home to Alanyaspor two weeks before the break. Genclerbirligi's own back line is thin, with Metehan and Diabate banned and Thalisson injured, so both nets look vulnerable.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners and I see no reason to move off that. Genclerbirligi should have more of the ball at Eryaman, but Gaziantep did push forward in their 2-0 home loss to Kasimpasa, hitting the woodwork twice, so both sides should earn a share.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards, already a busy line, and I lean a little higher. This is a relegation six-pointer, Genclerbirligi's last game brought a red card and a fifth-yellow suspension, and Gaziantep will be playing for a new or interim coach with nothing to protect.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots, which already allows for an open game. Tiago Gouveia, Franco Tongya and Pedro Mendes showed against Alanyaspor that Genclerbirligi can pile up chances at home, but Gaziantep have scored just twice in seven games, so I do not see the volume going much higher.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. I lean slightly higher because both defences are giving away clear chances: Gaziantep conceded twice to Kasimpasa inside 20 minutes, and Genclerbirligi will be patching up the middle of their defence.
